column1: If Logistic Regression already solves classification, why do we need Neural Networks?;Logistic Regression can only learn a linear decision boundary. Neural Networks can learn non-linear relationships by stacking layers with non-linear activation functions.

What does a neuron do in a Neural Network?;A neuron receives inputs, multiplies them by weights, optionally adds a bias, and passes the result through an activation function. The activation represents the neuron's output.

Why are activation functions necessary in Neural Networks?;Without activation functions, stacking multiple linear layers still produces a linear model. Activation functions introduce non-linearity, allowing the network to learn complex real-world relationships.

Why was Tanh introduced when Sigmoid already existed? What problem remained?;Sigmoid outputs 0 to 1 and is not zero-centered. Tanh outputs -1 to 1 and is zero-centered, but it can still saturate at -1 and 1, causing vanishing gradients.

How does ReLU work, and what problem does it address?;ReLU outputs 0 when z<0 and z when z>0. It introduces non-linearity while avoiding the saturation behavior of sigmoid/tanh on the positive side, helping reduce vanishing-gradient problems.
